question: In what ratio, wheat at ₹23 per kg should be mixed with wheat at ₹14 per kg so that on selling the mixture at ₹20 per kg there is a profit of 25%?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Cost Price (CP) of the mixture = 20 × (100 ÷ 125) = ₹16 per kg.

By alligation rule, Ratio = (16 − 14) ∶ (23 − 16) = 2 ∶ 7.

**∴ The correct answer is 2 ∶ 7.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Price of 1st variety of wheat = ₹23/kg

Price of 2ⁿd variety of wheat = ₹14/kg

Selling Price (SP) of the mixture = ₹20/kg

Profit = 25%

**Formula Used:**

CP = SP × [100 ÷ (100 + Profit%)]

Quantity 1 / Quantity 2 = (Mean CP − Price 2) / (Price 1 − Mean CP)
